html:
The War in Abkhazia was fought from 1992 to 1993 between Georgian government forces and Abkhaz separatists, backed by volunteers from the North Caucasus and by Russian forces, over the region of Abkhazia on the Black Sea.

The Abkhaz, a minority even in their own region, feared Georgian nationalism after independence. Georgian troops entered in August 1992, but in September 1993 the separatists took Sukhumi, and most of the region's Georgian population, around 200,000 people, fled or was expelled. Thousands died. Abkhazia has run itself since with Russian support, and Russia recognised it as independent after the war of 2008. The loss, along with South Ossetia, remains the main wound of modern Georgia, following the crisis of 1989.
